sources.title: Pueblo Günün a küna: ¿Kauchü kinawak?
sources.note: Community-authored self-description distinguishes the people, their Günün a atük homeland, and their Günün a yajüch language; includes contemporary written sample.

sources.title: Pueblo Günün a küna: Alfabeto
sources.note: Community account of the revitalization orthography, 2014 Gan Gan language meeting, and 2019 organizational adoption.

sources.title: Pueblo Günün a küna: Diccionario Günün a yajüch–Español
sources.note: Community-hosted, author-authorized vocabulary derived from the 2019 Shüptun–El eco language publication.

sources.title: Pueblo Günün a küna: Sierra y Laguna de los Padres activities
sources.note: Community report of 2025 ceremonial, educational, territorial care, and health-related collaboration.

sources.title: Pueblo Günün a küna: Manqueunai
sources.note: Community retelling of the seventeenth-century Manqueunai family, captivity, kinship, mourning, and Mascardi record with source caveats.

sources.title: Pueblo Günün a küna: Türatüra symbolism
sources.note: Community explanation of present-day transmitted symbolism and land concepts, not a dated 1492 artifact.

sources.title: Neuquén legislature: Günün a küna statement, 2019
sources.note: Official legislative transcript carries Indigenous self-description, homeland, language, historical names, and contemporary communities.

sources.title: Ver el mundo en Günün a yajüch
sources.note: 2026 ethnography with Günün a küna communities documents 2022–2025 language workshops, bilingual mapping, health, and reemergence.

sources.title: Turismo rural comunitario: una propuesta Günün a küna
sources.note: Community coauthors Norma Lucero and Daniel Huircapan document authority, educational fires, language work, and continuity.

sources.title: Descripción de la lengua Günün a iajüch
sources.note: Universidad Nacional del Sur linguistic thesis assesses historical documentation, contact, orthographic variation, grammar, and attribution limits.

sources.title: Corpus Histórico-Comparativo: Günün a Yajüch
sources.note: University linguistic project distinguishes Günün a Yajüch from Aonekko Aien and flags uncertain proposed family relationships.

sources.title: Contribución al estudio del indio Gününa Küne
sources.note: 1946 field records include speaker-consulted words, phrases, names, songs, oral accounts, and historically biased extinction language.

sources.title: Etnografía Gününa-Kena, 1958
sources.note: Later individual testimony requires time, informant, and racialized-title caveats; it does not establish all 1492 practices.

sources.title: El arte de las mujeres Aónik’enk y Gününa Küna
sources.note: Peer-reviewed 2002 study distinguishes traditions while examining women’s painted guanaco-skin cloaks and design histories.

sources.title: Pueblos Originarios: más de 6000 años en el Chubut inferior
sources.note: Regional education synthesis describes long Indigenous occupation and separately names Aónik’enk and Gününa Küna descendants.

sources.title: Los ríos en la arqueología de Norpatagonia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis of Colorado, Negro, and Chubut basins examines diverse settlement, resource, mortuary, and communication histories.

sources.title: El modo de vida cazador-recolector en el cuerpo del valle del Río Negro
sources.note: 2026 bioarchaeology abstract describes late-Holocene valley-centered mobility, plateau trips, guanaco, minor fauna, and wild plants.

sources.title: El uso de recursos vegetales en el este de Norpatagonia
sources.note: 2024 archaeology thesis identifies plant microremains, algarrobo and underground organs, and variable processing in Río Negro and Somuncurá.

sources.title: Cocina prehispánica del este de Norpatagonia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeological study of plant microremains at late-Holocene residential and mortuary Loma de los Muertos.

sources.title: Tecnología lítica de la costa centro-septentrional de Patagonia
sources.note: University thesis traces stone-tool design and regional contact north and south of the Chubut without ethnic attribution.

sources.title: Investigaciones arqueológicas en el valle medio-superior del río Negro
sources.note: University thesis surveys 21 sites, residential dunes, stone, pottery, beads, resources, exchange, and preservation limits.

sources.title: Fauna at Negro Muerto 3
sources.note: Peer-reviewed site study documents fish, mollusks, eggshell, reptiles, birds, mammals, cut marks, burning, and residential-mortuary contexts.

sources.title: Prehispanic pottery of the eastern northern Patagonia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis of Río Negro and San Blas ceramics uses petrography, residues, decoration, and chronology.

sources.title: Freshwater fauna in the lower Chubut valley
sources.note: Argentine archaeological study documents fish, waterfowl, coypu, and situational river resource use 1500–1200 years BP.

sources.title: Carbon isotopes and ceramic residues in northeast Chubut
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis supports mixed marine-terrestrial diets including guanaco, mollusks, plants, pinnipeds, and seasonal variation.

sources.title: Somuncurá circulation and exchange indicators
sources.note: University archaeological research examines recurring plateau use, raw materials, projectiles, ceramics, and changing exchange networks.

sources.title: Arid central Río Negro site fauna and water
sources.note: Regional archaeology abstract describes occupation near a temporary reservoir and spring; dating remains uncertain.

sources.title: Mortuary record and mobility in northwest Patagonia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed regional article addresses varied late-Holocene mortuary treatment and uncertain mobility interpretations.

sources.title: Los caciques del Río Negro a fines del siglo XVIII
sources.note: Ethnohistorian Lidia Nacuzzi documents mobile, shifting alliances and imposed colonial labels; warns against projection to 1492.

sources.title: Repensando el concepto de cacicazgo en Pampa y Patagonia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed reassessment of eighteenth-century indigenous leadership, transformation, and limits of fixed chiefdom models.

sources.title: INAI recognizes Indigenous-language health translations
sources.note: Argentine Indigenous affairs agency identifies Günün a küna translator Daniel Huircapan in 2021 public-health translation.

sources.title: INCUAPA: ancestral DNA community meeting
sources.note: CONICET account distinguishes participating Chewelche, Günün a küna, Mapuche, and Rankülche communities and records consent.

sources.title: Nuevas investigaciones del Túmulo de Malacara
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeology discusses uncertain mound interpretation and contemporary Külüla a Küna memorial and seasonal ceremonies.

sources.title: Buenos Aires health materials translated to Indigenous languages
sources.note: Provincial public-health agency documents 2021 Günün a Küna language vaccination materials and present distribution.

sources.title: COVID-19 and Indigenous peoples of Argentina, second-stage report
sources.note: Collaborative 2020 report includes Günün a küna families’ own account of recognition, language learning, water, health, and discrimination.

sources.title: Murales por la Memoria: pueblos originarios
sources.note: Argentine public-history account dates 1878–1885 military campaign, dispossession, confinement, and false empty-desert narrative.

sources.title: INAI Resolution 363/2015
sources.note: Official registration of a specifically named mixed Mapuche-Tehuelche community; identity is not generalized to all Günün a küna.

sources.title: II Jornada de Revitalización Lingüística program
sources.note: University program identifies Daniel Huircapan and separately describes Aonekko Aien language work.

sources.title: Argentina 2022 census Indigenous methods
sources.note: National statistics methods credit a Günün a küna authority in Indigenous self-identification coding and language questions.

sources.title: Üyüy a jüchü / La voz del viento
sources.note: University publisher presents Daniel Huircapan’s 2022 bilingual ancestral-story book and contemporary language use.

sources.title: Oral pathologies in the Pampa-Patagonia transition
sources.note: Peer-reviewed late-Holocene lower Colorado River dental study documents caries, abscesses, calculus, and dietary limits.

sources.title: Infancias y niñeces en cazadores-recolectores de Patagonia
sources.note: Research conference methodology addresses preservation bias in nonadult mortuary evidence; cannot reconstruct named childcare from it.

sources.title: El trabajo del cuero en Campo Moncada 2
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Chubut valley archaeology documents hide-working tools and material practices without assigning an ethnicity.

sources.title: Vocabulario en idioma Günün a yajüch
sources.note: Argentine cultural sound archive attributes a 2018 community teaching recording to Daniel Huircapan.
